dataset.name: Amazon Reviews 2023
dataset.proxy_labeling_notice: Labels mapped from star ratings (1-2 neg, 3 neu, 4-5 pos). Reflects real transactional proxy sentiment.

model.selected_model: TF-IDF (20k, Stopwords Preserved) + Calibrated Linear SVM (C=0.5)
model.vectorizer: Optimized TF-IDF (20,000 features, 1-2 ngrams, sublinear_tf, stopwords preserved)

model_comparison.model_name: TF-IDF (20k, Stopwords Preserved) + Calibrated Linear SVM (C=0.5)
TF-IDF (20k, Stopwords Preserved) + Soft Voting Ensemble (LR + SVM)

neutral_class_analysis.finding: Neutral (3-star) reviews exhibit significantly higher label noise than polarized reviews. Of the 1,500 held-out neutral reviews, 23.5% were classified as negative and 11.9% as positive, reflecting customer tendency to assign 3 stars to mixed reviews containing explicit polarity phrases.
neutral_class_analysis.mixed_signals_note: Star ratings represent overall satisfaction, not strict linguistic neutrality.

binary_benchmark.task: Binary Sentiment Classification (1-2 Stars Negative vs 4-5 Stars Positive, 3-Star Excluded)
binary_benchmark.note: Separate benchmark excluding ambiguous 3-star reviews. Demonstrates that sentiment polarity achieves 93.70% test accuracy when ambiguous neutral proxy labels are removed.

limitations: Star ratings represent customer satisfaction rather than linguistic sentiment alone.
Neutral class exhibits lower recall (64.7%) due to inherent mixed-sentiment ambiguity in 3-star reviews.
Domain-specific terminology reflects consumer appliances and e-commerce vocabulary.

DistilBERT transformer fine-tuning was constrained by Python 3.14 CPU environment without pre-built Windows torch wheels; optimized linear model achieved 75.82% 3-class accuracy with sub-millisecond CPU latency.
